Which of the following statements is true about a credit risk model with high precision?
options: It correctly identifies a high percentage of non-risky customers out of all actual non-risky cases.
It correctly identifies a high percentage of non-risky customers out of all predicted non-risky cases.
It correctly identifies a high percentage of risky customers out of all actual risky cases.
It correctly identifies a high percentage of risky customers out of all predicted risky cases.
questions.correct_answer: It correctly identifies a high percentage of risky customers out of all predicted risky cases.

questions.text: If a credit risk model's recall is 0.7 and precision is 0.5, what can be inferred about its performance?
options: The model identifies 70% of all actual risky customers and 50% of its positive predictions are correct.
The model identifies 50% of all actual risky customers and 70% of its positive predictions are correct.
The model has a high false positive rate and a low false negative rate.
The model has a low false positive rate and a high false negative rate.
questions.correct_answer: The model identifies 70% of all actual risky customers and 50% of its positive predictions are correct.

questions.text: In a SHAP waterfall plot, what does the initial value represent?
options: The average prediction of the model
The model’s output without any feature contributions
The model’s prediction before adding any feature contributions
The overall importance of each feature
questions.correct_answer: The model’s prediction before adding any feature contributions

questions.text: How does SHAP facilitate global interpretability of a model?
options: By providing exact feature importance scores for individual predictions
By aggregating local SHAP values to estimate the global importance of each feature across all predictions
By displaying only the top features contributing to the model’s predictions
By creating visualizations that show how features impact model accuracy
questions.correct_answer: By aggregating local SHAP values to estimate the global importance of each feature across all predictions

Which statement concerning the net present value (NPV) of an investment or a financing project is correct?
options: A financing project should be accepted if, and only if, the NPV is exactly equal to zero.
An investment project should be accepted only if the NPV is equal to the initial cash flow.
Any type of project should be accepted if the NPV is positive and rejected if it is negative.
Any type of project with greater total cash inflows than total cash outflows, should always be accepted.
questions.correct_answer: Any type of project should be accepted if the NPV is positive and rejected if it is negative.

questions.text: Wilson's Market is considering two mutually exclusive projects that will not be repeated. The required rate of return is 13.9 percent for Project A and 12.5 percent for Project B. Project A has an initial cost of ₹54,500, and should produce cash inflows of ₹16,400, ₹28,900, and ₹31,700 for Years 1 to 3, respectively. Project B has an initial cost of ₹69,400, and should produce cash inflows of ₹0, ₹48,300, and ₹42,100, for Years 1 to 3, respectively. Which project, or projects, if either, should be accepted and why?___________________
options: Project A; because its NPV is positive while Project B's NPV is negative
Project A; because it has the higher required rate of return
Project B; because it has the largest total cash inflow
Neither project; because neither has an NPV equal to or greater than its initial cost
questions.correct_answer: Project A; because its NPV is positive while Project B's NPV is negative
